title: Giant-atom-mediated photon blockade
authors: C. Cui, W. Y. Hu, Y. Q. Ji, H. T. Cui, Yan-Hui Zhou, H. Z. Shen
abstract: Photon blockade is a phenomenon where the presence of system nonlinearity causes the output to consist of single photons, which has been extensively studied in point atom systems, but it is barely explored in giant atom ones. In this paper, we propose giant atom-mediated photon blockade scheme based on two cavities and three cavities systems with driving field applied to the first cavity. We show that simultaneous unconventional photon blockades (UPBs) can not occur in the point atom system (the atom coupling only to the leftmost cavity) due to there always existing a cavity to have a single path. In contrast, the spatially extended nature of giant atom enables coupling to multiple cavities and allows for the introduction of a phase and coupling strength. Consequently, simultaneous UPBs in multiple cavities can be obtained due to the multipath destructive interference. Moreover, by manipulating the detuning, we observe simultaneous conventional photon blockades (CPBs) in multiple cavities. Finally, we study simultaneous two-photon blockades (2PBs) in point atom multiple cavities system.
summary: This paper explores photon blockade in quantum systems using giant atoms coupled to multiple optical cavities. It demonstrates that the extended nature of these atoms enables the simultaneous occurrence of unconventional and conventional photon blockades through destructive interference pathways. The theoretical analysis uses master equations and $g^{(2)}(0)$ measurements to map out the required physical parameters for this advanced quantum control.
main_problem: The paper investigates the realization and control of simultaneous unconventional and conventional photon blockades in quantum systems mediated by giant atoms.
main_result: The spatially extended nature of giant atoms allows for simultaneous photon blockades (both conventional and unconventional) in multiple coupled cavities via multipath destructive interference, a feat impossible in simple point atom systems.
method: The analysis uses the Lindblad master equation to model system dynamics and calculates the second-order correlation function, g^(2)(0), to diagnose photon statistics.
model_or_system: The system consists of a giant atom coupled to two or three optical cavities. The Hamiltonian and dynamics are described using cavity and atomic coupling strengths, detunings, and driving fields.
key_observables: Second-order correlation function g^(2)(0) (where < 1 indicates blockade), and the detection of simultaneous CPBs and UPBs.
important_parameters: Cavity frequencies ($\omega_j$), atom transition frequency ($\omega_0$), coupling strengths ($J, V$), inter-cavity coupling ($\lambda$), and detuning ($\Delta$).
main_assumptions: Dissipation rates are often assumed equal ($\kappa_1 = \kappa_2 = \kappa_3 = \gamma$), and specific resonance conditions are used for detailed blockade analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic coupling structures, level diagrams showing CPB mechanisms, and plots of log10 g^(2)(0) vs. detuning/coupling strength demonstrating the optimal conditions for simultaneous blockades.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the general Hamiltonian and master equation for $N=2$ and $N=3$ cavities, to deriving the diagnostic tool $g^{(2)}(0)$, and finally demonstrating the physical mechanisms and optimal parameters for achieving simultaneous CPBs and UPBs.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses advanced topics in cavity QED and open quantum systems by extending blockade phenomena from simple point atoms to complex, spatially extended giant atoms, opening new avenues for quantum light sources.
